title: Documentation drift review
summary: Compare documentation and architecture notes with the code they describe, and flag claims that overstate what is implemented.

provenance.notes: Mirrors an observed failure in this project: documents describing guarantees (shared reviewer context, strict verifier permissions) the code did not yet provide.

outputs.name: drift
outputs.description: Claims not supported by code, code behavior not documented, and stale commands.

workflow.step: Extract every checkable claim: guarantees, commands, file paths, names, defaults, limits.
workflow.check: Claims are quoted with their location.

workflow.step: Verify each against the code or by checking that the command and path exist; mark verified, contradicted or unverifiable.
workflow.check: No claim is marked verified without a file reference.

workflow.step: Flag claims stronger than the implementation, such as 'always', 'guarantees' or 'prevents' where the code only checks in some paths.
workflow.check: Absolute words are traced to enforcing code.

workflow.step: Separate implemented behavior from proposed or deferred work and make the document say which is which.
Propose minimal edits; do not rewrite unrelated sections.

constraints: Do not add stray Markdown beside code; follow the repository's documentation layout.
Do not describe a smoke test as passed when it was deferred.
Keep edits within the documents in scope.

examples.title: Overstated guarantee
examples.situation: A document says every reviewer receives the pinned design, but one path does not pass it.
examples.guidance: Report as contradicted, cite the path, and reword the document or fix the code in a separate task.

verification: Each finding quotes the claim and cites the contradicting or missing code.
Commands in the document were checked to exist.

task.text: Check the docs for stale claims that overstate the guarantee versus the code.
Update the readme and runbook after the change.
